name: Alabama Public Service Commission
selectionDetail: Statewide partisan elections for President, Place 1 and Place 2 (4-year terms); governor fills vacancies by appointment. HB 475 (signed April 2026) expands the commission to seven members: Gov. Ivey appointed four additional commissioners (two from majority-party and two from minority-party legislative nominations) effective Jan. 18, 2027, and future seats move to congressional-district elections.
electionMechanism: Place 1 and Place 2 are directly elected statewide on 2026-11-03; both incumbents lost GOP primaries. Place 1: Matt Gentry (R) vs. James Gordon (D). Place 2: Jim Zeigler (R) vs. Sheila McNeil (D). President seat (Almond, appointed June 2025) is not on the 2026 ballot. Separately, four governor-appointed members created by HB 475 join on Jan. 18, 2027, so the 2026 winners will be 2 of 7 commissioners.

Lee is term-limited), so the governor elected in Nov. 2026 will fill gubernatorial seats as they come open (Jones was reappointed by Gov. Lee in 2024; Hilliard was reappointed in 2023). Legislative seats are appointed by the speakers, who are chosen by chambers whose House seats and half of whose Senate seats are on the 2026 ballot. No specific seat was verified to expire in 2027.

name: Vermont Public Utility Commission
selectionDetail: Chair nominated, appointed and confirmed in the manner of a Superior judge. For the two members, the governor submits at least five names to the Judicial Nominating Board, which reviews and recommends, and the governor appoints (30 V.S.A. § 3). Six-year terms.
electionMechanism: Governor appoints through the Judicial Nominating Board process; Vermont elects its governor every two years, and the governor's race is on the 2026 ballot. Riley Allen's term runs 2021-2027, so the governor elected in Nov. 2026 makes the next scheduled appointment (or reappointment).
